symptom: PC1 in office VLAN 10 cannot ping PC2 in the same office, both on SW1.
topology_note: SW1 access ports Fa0/1 (PC1) and Fa0/2 (PC2), both meant to be VLAN 10.
show_output: show vlan brief: VLAN10 ACTIVE Fa0/1; Fa0/2 NOT listed under VLAN10, shows under VLAN1. show run int fa0/2: switchport access vlan 1.
expected_fault: Fa0/2 was left in default VLAN 1 instead of being assigned to VLAN 10, so PC2 is on a different broadcast domain than PC1.

symptom: Two new PCs on SW2 cannot reach anything, including each other.
topology_note: Ports Fa0/5 and Fa0/6 were configured for VLAN 30 (new Sales VLAN).
show_output: show vlan brief: VLAN30 does not appear in the table at all. show run int fa0/5: switchport access vlan 30 (command accepted, but vlan 30 was never created with 'vlan 30' global command).
expected_fault: VLAN 30 was assigned to ports but never created on the switch, so those ports are effectively inactive/blackholed.

symptom: VLAN 20 devices on SW1 can reach the router but VLAN 20 devices on SW2 cannot.
topology_note: SW1-SW2 link is a trunk carrying VLAN 10/20/30.
show_output: SW1 show int trunk: Fa0/24 native vlan 1. SW2 show int trunk: Fa0/24 native vlan 99. CDP native VLAN mismatch warning logged.
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch on the trunk (VLAN 1 vs VLAN 99) is causing VLAN 20 traffic to be mishandled across the trunk.

symptom: Printer on Fa0/8 is unreachable from the Accounting VLAN.
topology_note: Printer should be in VLAN 40 (Accounting) alongside the rest of the department.
show_output: show vlan brief: Fa0/8 listed under VLAN 1. show run int fa0/8: no switchport access vlan command present (still default).
expected_fault: Fa0/8 was never explicitly assigned to VLAN 40 and is still sitting in default VLAN 1.

symptom: Entire VLAN 10 subnet is unreachable from every other VLAN.
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick with subinterfaces per VLAN on Gi0/0.
show_output: show ip interface brief: Gi0/0.10 10.10.10.1 administratively down. show run: interface Gi0/0.10 ... shutdown.
expected_fault: The VLAN 10 router subinterface (Gi0/0.10) is administratively shut down, taking the whole VLAN off the network.

symptom: PC3 can ping other hosts on its own subnet but nothing off-subnet.
topology_note: PC3 is on 192.168.5.0/24 behind R1's Gi0/1.
show_output: PC3 ipconfig: IP 192.168.5.50/24, gateway 192.168.6.1. R1 show ip int brief: Gi0/1 192.168.5.1/24 up/up.
expected_fault: PC3's default gateway (192.168.6.1) is not on its own subnet and does not match the router's real interface (192.168.5.1).

symptom: New laptop can ping the router's LAN IP but not the internet or other VLANs.
topology_note: Static IP was configured by hand on the laptop.
show_output: Laptop ipconfig: IP 172.16.1.100/24, gateway 172.16.1.001 (typo, should be .1). Router Gi0/0: 172.16.1.1/24 up/up.
expected_fault: The gateway address was mistyped (172.16.1.001) so it never resolves to the router's real interface.

symptom: Whole branch office lost connectivity to HQ at the same time.
topology_note: Branch router R2 Gi0/1 is the LAN gateway for 10.20.0.0/24.
show_output: R2 show ip int brief: Gi0/1 10.20.0.1 down/down (line protocol down). show log: %LINK-3-UPDOWN Gi0/1 changed state to down.
expected_fault: The gateway interface Gi0/1 itself is physically/line-protocol down, so no host behind it can reach anything.

symptom: PC5 can reach some hosts on its floor but not the gateway or anything beyond.
topology_note: Floor uses 192.168.20.0/25 (mask .128), split into two half-subnets.
expected_fault: PC5 has the wrong subnet mask (/24 instead of /25), so it thinks the gateway is on-link when it is actually in a different /25 block on the wire.

symptom: New PCs in the lab get an APIPA 169.254.x.x address instead of a real IP.
topology_note: Lab VLAN 50 uses DHCP pool LAB50, 50 addresses reserved.
show_output: show ip dhcp pool LAB50: leased 50, total 50 (0 available). debug ip dhcp server events: DHCPDISCOVER, no addresses available.
expected_fault: The DHCP scope for VLAN 50 is fully exhausted, so new clients fall back to APIPA.

symptom: PC gets an IP that collides with the router's own interface address.
topology_note: Router Gi0/0 is 10.10.60.1, DHCP pool covers 10.10.60.0/24.
show_output: show run: ip dhcp excluded-address command is missing for 10.10.60.1-10.10.60.10. show ip dhcp binding: 10.10.60.1 leased to PC-MAC-aa:bb.
expected_fault: The router's own gateway address was never excluded from the DHCP pool, so it was handed out to a client, creating an address conflict.

symptom: Clients on a remote VLAN never get an address; DHCP server is centralized on another subnet.
topology_note: VLAN 70 clients, DHCP server lives on VLAN 1 attached to R1.
show_output: R1 show run int vlan70: no ip helper-address configured. debug ip dhcp: no DHCPDISCOVER ever reaches the server interface.
expected_fault: Missing 'ip helper-address' on the VLAN 70 gateway interface means broadcast DHCPDISCOVER packets never reach the remote DHCP server.

symptom: Clients get an IP address but internet browsing fails immediately.
topology_note: DHCP pool LAB80 configured recently by a junior admin.
show_output: show run: ip dhcp pool LAB80 ... default-router 10.10.80.254 (router's real interface is 10.10.80.1).
expected_fault: The DHCP pool advertises the wrong default-router option, handing clients a gateway address that does not exist on the segment.

symptom: Users can ping the web server by IP but browsing by hostname fails.
topology_note: Internal DNS server is 10.10.1.53.
show_output: PC nslookup intranet.local: Request timed out. PC ping 10.10.1.53: Request timed out. PC ping 10.10.5.20 (web server IP): success.
expected_fault: The DNS server 10.10.1.53 is unreachable, so name resolution fails even though IP connectivity to the actual service is fine.

symptom: Only one PC in the lab cannot resolve any hostname; others are fine.
topology_note: DHCP normally hands out DNS 10.10.1.53, this PC has a static config.
show_output: PC ipconfig /all: DNS Server 10.10.1.35 (transposed digits, should be .53). ping 10.10.1.35: Destination host unreachable.
expected_fault: A statically configured DNS server address has a digit transposition (10.10.1.35 vs 10.10.1.53) pointing at a nonexistent host.

symptom: Branch office cannot resolve HQ hostnames even though the DNS server IP is reachable.
topology_note: An ACL was recently added to the WAN link for security hardening.
show_output: ping 10.10.1.53 from branch: success. nslookup: Request timed out. show access-lists WAN-IN: deny udp any any eq 53 (line 10) present above any permit.
expected_fault: A newly added ACL entry is blocking UDP port 53 (DNS) across the WAN link, even though basic ICMP reachability still works.

symptom: New internal app server can't be reached by name, only by IP.
topology_note: Server was just deployed at 10.10.9.30.
show_output: nslookup appserver.local: Non-existent domain. DNS server show zone internal.local: no A record for appserver.
expected_fault: No DNS A record was ever created for the new server, so the name simply does not exist in the zone.

symptom: HQ can ping the branch router's WAN interface but not any branch LAN host.
topology_note: Branch LAN is 172.20.5.0/24, advertised via static routes at HQ.
show_output: HQ show ip route: no entry for 172.20.5.0/24. show run: missing 'ip route 172.20.5.0 255.255.255.0 <branch-wan-ip>' statement.
expected_fault: HQ is missing the static route to the branch LAN subnet (172.20.5.0/24), so return traffic has no path back.

symptom: Two areas that used to see each other's routes suddenly stopped exchanging routes.
topology_note: R1 and R2 run OSPF area 0 over a shared /30 link.
show_output: R1 show ip ospf neighbor: (empty, no neighbors). show run int Gi0/1: ip ospf 1 area 0 present, but 'ip address' shows a typo'd /29 instead of /30 mask, breaking the adjacency.
expected_fault: A subnet mask mismatch on the OSPF link (/29 vs /30) is preventing the OSPF neighbor adjacency from forming.

symptom: Traffic to the internet times out even though the default route exists.
topology_note: R1 has a static default route pointing to the ISP.
show_output: show ip route: S* 0.0.0.0/0 via 203.0.113.254. ping 203.0.113.254: Request timed out (that address is not the ISP's real next hop, which is .254 vs actual .253).
expected_fault: The default route's next-hop IP (203.0.113.254) is wrong; the real ISP hand-off address is 203.0.113.253, so the route points at a dead end.

symptom: Ping between two sites works one way and fails the other way.
topology_note: Two ISP links provide redundancy; policy routing was recently added.
show_output: Traceroute site A to B: completes normally. Traceroute site B to A: dies at the last hop. show route-map POLICY: return path forced out the wrong interface.
expected_fault: A policy-based routing map is sending return traffic out a different, misconfigured interface, creating asymmetric routing that breaks the reverse path.

symptom: HR VLAN can no longer reach the payroll server after a new ACL was applied.
topology_note: ACL PAYROLL-IN applied inbound on the payroll server's VLAN interface.
show_output: show access-lists PAYROLL-IN: permit tcp 10.10.11.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.10.99.5 eq 443 (only). show access-lists hit counts: implicit deny counter incrementing heavily.
expected_fault: The new ACL only permits HTTPS (443) and everything else, including the app's real port (8443), is caught by the implicit deny at the end of the list.

symptom: A specific host that should be blocked from the server VLAN can still get through.
topology_note: ACL is supposed to deny host 10.10.12.50 but permit the rest of the subnet.
show_output: show access-lists BLOCK-HOST: line 10 permit ip 10.10.12.0 0.0.0.255 any; line 20 deny host 10.10.12.50 any. Deny line never matches because the broader permit is evaluated first.
expected_fault: ACL statement order is wrong: the broad permit for the whole subnet comes before the specific deny, so the deny for 10.10.12.50 never gets evaluated.

symptom: Outbound web browsing from the lab VLAN works, but nobody outside can reach the lab's test web server.
topology_note: ACL LAB-ACL was intended to allow inbound HTTP to the test server only.
show_output: show run int vlan90: ip access-group LAB-ACL out (applied outbound instead of inbound). show access-lists LAB-ACL: permit tcp any host 10.10.90.20 eq 80.
expected_fault: The ACL was applied in the 'out' direction on the VLAN interface instead of 'in', so it never filters the inbound traffic it was written for.

symptom: Outbound DNS queries from a locked-down VLAN work, but no answers ever come back.
topology_note: A restrictive numbered ACL only lists specific permits with no 'established' or return-traffic allowance.
show_output: show access-lists 101: permit udp 10.10.13.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 53 (outbound only, standard ACL cannot match return traffic by state).
expected_fault: The ACL only permits outbound DNS queries; because it is a standard/stateless list with no matching return-traffic entry, DNS responses are dropped.

symptom: No internal host can reach the internet even though the default route and ISP link are up.
topology_note: PAT/NAT overload is configured on R1 for internet access.
show_output: show run: ip nat inside source list 1 interface Gi0/0 overload present. show ip interface: Gi0/1 (LAN) NOT marked 'NAT: inside'. Gi0/0 (WAN) NOT marked 'NAT: outside'.
expected_fault: The 'ip nat inside' and 'ip nat outside' interface commands were never applied, so the NAT overload rule has no interfaces to actually translate on.

symptom: Only a handful of PCs can browse the internet; the rest of the subnet cannot.
topology_note: NAT overload uses access-list 1 to define which hosts get translated.
show_output: show access-lists 1: permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.15 (only covers .0-.15, subnet is actually /24). show ip nat translations: only low-numbered hosts appear.
expected_fault: The NAT source access-list only matches the first 16 addresses of the subnet (wrong wildcard mask), so the rest of the LAN is never translated.

symptom: Internal web server is reachable from inside but not from the internet.
topology_note: Server should be reachable via a static NAT/port-forward on TCP 80.
show_output: show run: no 'ip nat inside source static tcp 10.10.5.20 80 interface Gi0/0 80' entry present. show ip nat translations: no static entries for 10.10.5.20.
expected_fault: No static NAT/port-forward rule exists for the web server, so inbound requests from outside have no translation to reach it.

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi devices can reach internal file servers, which should never happen.
topology_note: Guest SSID is supposed to map to VLAN 99, isolated by an ACL.
show_output: show wlan 2 (Guest): interface VLAN10 (should be VLAN99). VLAN10 is the trusted internal VLAN with no isolation ACL.
expected_fault: The Guest SSID is mapped to VLAN 10 (internal) instead of VLAN 99 (isolated guest), so guest traffic lands directly on the trusted network.

symptom: Several students' laptops fail to join the classroom Wi-Fi with an authentication error, others connect fine.
topology_note: WPA2-Enterprise SSID re-keyed recently for the semester.
show_output: WLC client trap log: repeated 802.1X authentication failures for a subset of MAC addresses. Those laptops still have last semester's cached RADIUS credentials/profile.
expected_fault: Affected laptops are using a stale cached Wi-Fi profile with last semester's 802.1X credentials, which no longer match the RADIUS server.
